# v0.3.0 — Cleaning feedback, browser-close helper and registry safety net

## Progress you can watch

Every cleanup — moving files to the trash, purging browser caches, fixing
registry issues — now shows a **determinate progress overlay** with a live
counter, handing over to the success toast when done. The backend reports
progress at ~1% steps, so even a hundred-thousand-item trash job never turns
into an IPC storm.

## Close your browsers before cleaning (with one click)

Browser caches can only be fully cleaned when the browser is not holding the
files open. The cache cleaning dialog now warns about it and offers a
**"Close browsers" button** that gracefully quits every running browser —
SIGTERM on Linux, `taskkill` WM_CLOSE on Windows, an AppleScript quit on
macOS. Sessions are saved; the toast reports which browsers were closed.

## Registry fixes now require a backup (Windows)

Fixing registry issues is no longer a leap of faith. Before any fix is
applied, and **without exceptions**:

1. **A .reg backup of every affected key** is exported to
   `registry-backups/backup-<timestamp>/` (with a manifest mapping files to
   keys). Any export failure aborts the fix — nothing is touched.
2. **A system restore point** is created through a single UAC prompt (which
   also lifts Windows' once-per-24h restore-point throttle). Declining the
   prompt or having System Restore disabled aborts the fix with a clear
   message.

The success toast shows where the backup lives, and the confirmation dialog
tells you upfront what will happen.

## Windows-only registry entry

The Registry page only makes sense on Windows, so the sidebar entry and the
results filter for registry issues are now hidden on Linux and macOS
instead of leading to a dead end.
